glossary.definition: An organised human society with settled cities, farming, rulers, skilled craftworkers, and shared writing.
The yearly summer flooding of the River Nile that soaked Egypt's dry valley and left behind rich dark mud.
The Ancient Egyptians' name for their fertile Nile valley, meaning Black Land after the dark flood silt where crops grew.
The Ancient Egyptians' name for the scorching, dry Sahara desert beyond the river valley, meaning Red Land.
A hand-operated wooden lever with a bucket on one end and a heavy mud weight on the other for lifting Nile water onto fields.
A tall triangular marsh reed growing beside the River Nile, woven into boats, sandals, ropes, and smooth writing sheets.
The combined red-and-white royal crown worn after King Narmer united northern Lower Egypt and southern Upper Egypt around 3100 BC.
The supreme ruler of Ancient Egypt, honoured by Egyptians as both a royal monarch and a living god on earth.
The brilliant royal architect who stacked six stone layers at Saqqara around 2670 BC to build Pharaoh Djoser's Step Pyramid.
A giant four-sided stone royal tomb rising to a pointed peak, built during the Old Kingdom to protect a Pharaoh's body forever.
An open rock cliff or pit where Egyptian stonemasons cut heavy limestone and granite blocks using copper chisels and wooden wedges.
A giant carved stone guardian statue combining the strong body of a crouching lion with the head of a Pharaoh, such as Khafre's Great Sphinx at Giza.
The Pharaoh's highest royal official and chief minister, trusted to oversee judges, tax records, and royal grain stores.
A trained Egyptian reader and writer who studied for years to paint hieroglyphs and ink records on papyrus scrolls.
Ancient Egypt's sacred writing system of more than 700 picture and sound signs carved into temple stone or painted in ink.
A popular Ancient Egyptian board game in which two players tossed flat throwing sticks to race counters across thirty squares.
An oval loop with a knotted line at one end drawn around the sacred hieroglyphic name of a Pharaoh or queen, vital for decoding the Rosetta Stone.
Believing in and worshipping many different gods and goddesses, such as Ra, Osiris, Isis, Horus, Thoth, and Anubis.
Preserving a dead body over seventy days by drying it in desert salt, rubbing sweet oils on the skin, and wrapping tight linen bandages.
Natural dry desert salt packed over and inside a dead body for forty days during mummification to soak up moisture and stop decay.
Four carved stone jars with guardian-headed lids used by priests to store the dried lungs, stomach, liver, and intestines safely inside a tomb.
Small glazed clay or wooden servant figures placed inside tombs to wake up magically and do farm work for their owner in the afterlife.
The Egyptian goddess and sacred idea of truth, fairness, and balance, whose light feather was weighed against each dead person's heart.
Powerful female New Kingdom Pharaoh who ruled Egypt peacefully around 1479 BC, wore royal kingly symbols, and sent five trading ships to the Land of Punt.
A light, fast two-wheeled wooden war cart pulled by two galloping horses and crewed by a driver and an archer, raced at the Battle of Kadesh.
A hidden desert canyon near Thebes where New Kingdom Pharaohs such as Tutankhamun cut secret rock tombs deep inside limestone cliffs.
A heavy carved stone outer coffin placed inside a royal burial chamber to hold nested gilded wooden coffins and protect the mummy.
Relating to the Greek-speaking royal dynasty started by General Ptolemy after 323 BC and ended when Queen Cleopatra VII was defeated by Rome in 30 BC.

concept_widget.title: Weighing the Heart on Anubis's Golden Scales: Heart vs Feather of Ma'at
concept_widget.caption: Tap each stage inside the Hall of Two Truths to see how Anubis, Thoth, Ammit, and Osiris judged every spirit.

eras.headline: Anubis Places the Heart Opposite Ma'at's Feather
eras.summary: Guided by painted Book of the Dead scrolls into the Hall of Two Truths, jackal-headed Anubis placed the dead person's heart on golden scales opposite Ma'at's light feather of truth while Thoth stood ready to write.

pillars.status: Placed on the Golden Scale Dish
Sacred Measure of Truth and Kindness

eras.headline: Light and Balanced: Welcome to the Sunny Field of Reeds!
eras.summary: When a person lived honestly and kindly, their heart stayed as light as Ma'at's feather of truth! Ibis-headed Thoth recorded the fair result, and green-skinned Osiris welcomed them into the sunny Field of Reeds forever.

pillars.status: Osiris Opens the Field of Reeds

eras.headline: Tipped by Mean Deeds: Gobbled Up by Fierce Ammit!
eras.summary: If a heart was heavy with mean deeds, it tipped the golden scales down below Ma'at's light feather! Waiting beside the scales crouched fierce Ammit — part crocodile, lion, and hippo — who gobbled the heavy heart up.

pillars.status: Tips the Scales and Gobbled by Ammit

source_texts.text: Artefact note: Look closely at the horizontal bands across this cracked tan tablet. A temple scribe rolled tiny standing figures across damp mud and pressed neat wedge-shaped reed marks to count barley.

Artefact note: Follow the long sloping wooden beam from the gardener's hands up past the leafy fruit trees to its rounded back end. Below his bare feet sits a collared brown dog beside lotus-filled water.

Artefact note: This close-up carving on dark green siltstone shows a barefoot royal attendant carrying a small washing pot and woven sandals beneath a flower sign, walking right behind the giant figure on the palette.

Artefact note: Notice the flat, pale top surface and rough, shell-speckled sides of this thick yellow-brown Giza limestone block. Even one single stone from Khufu's tomb weighs as much as a family car.
Artefact note: Trace this solid metal bar from its narrow, flattened striking end on the left to its gently curved cutting edge on the right, now speckled green after thousands of years.

Artefact note: Carved from glossy dark diorite stone, Pharaoh Khafre sits bolt upright wearing a pleated kilt and royal headcloth. Look right behind his neck, where carved bird wings curve around his head.

Artefact note: Three bands cross this broken dark grey slab — tiny picture signs at the top, quick everyday script in the middle, and capital letters below. Its final carved line orders: "Set up this hard stone in three scripts."

Artefact note: Look closely at the criss-cross plant fibres on this golden-tan papyrus sheet. Two neat columns of flowing ink signs run from right to left, switching smoothly between dark black soot and bright red headings.

Artefact note: Three neat rows of ten turquoise-blue glazed squares run across the top of this hollow game box. Notice the open sliding drawer at the back left and the cone-shaped and spool-shaped playing pieces.

Artefact note: Cast in dark bronze with gleaming touches of gold leaf on his wig and kilt, tall prick-eared Anubis strides forward on a hieroglyph-carved base towards two cobras and a tiny kneeling worshipper.
Artefact note: Fine tool marks still show down the tall, hollowed cream-white limestone body of this tomb jar, topped by a snug stone lid carved with the calm human face of guardian Imsety.

Artefact note: Shaped like a tiny wrapped mummy in shiny turquoise glaze, this hand-sized clay figure wears a black-striped wig, crosses both arms over its chest, and carries two columns of ink hieroglyphs.

Artefact note: Seated calmly on a solid stone throne carved with royal hieroglyphs beside her legs, female ruler Hatshepsut wears the wide striped headcloth, brow cobra, and pleated kilt usually reserved for Egypt's male kings.

Artefact note: Original mineral paint still glows after three thousand years on this sculpted limestone portrait, from the red-and-green ribbon around her tall flat-topped crown down to the rows of petals across her shoulders.

Artefact note: Tiny wedge-shaped signs fill this cracked terracotta clay tablet and its smaller matching corner fragment below. Its carved lines record King Hattusili and Pharaoh Ramesses promising: "He is a brother to me, and I am a brother to him."

Artefact note: Under a bright lamp inside the rock-cut burial chamber, two turbaned Egyptian specialists, a colleague, and Howard Carter on the right steady wooden beams and padded blocks beneath the curved golden shrine roof.

Artefact note: Sheet gold, deep-blue glass, and polished stones still shine brightly on this royal backrest, where Queen Ankhesenamun holds a tiny perfume cup and gently touches young Tutankhamun's collar beneath golden sunbeams.
Artefact note: Struck into solid silver inside a dotted border, Queen Cleopatra VII faces right wearing her wavy hair in a neat braided bun bound with the broad cloth headband of Greek monarchs.
